name: Sales — competitor follower
description: For people following or engaging with a competitor. Never names the competitor and never rubbishes them — that reads as insecurity. Leads with the category problem instead.
audience: Lists built from a competitor's company followers or the engagers on a competitor's posts.

variants: {{firstName|Hi}} — you clearly pay attention to this category, which is rarer than it should be. Connecting to follow what {{company|your team}} is doing with it.
Hi {{firstName|there}} — we work in the same category you're evidently tracking. Would be good to be connected.
Thanks {{firstName|there}}. Since you're evaluating this space — what's the thing none of the tools you've looked at actually do? That answer is worth more to me than a demo slot.
Straight question, {{firstName|there}}: what did the tools you've tried get wrong? I'd rather hear that than pitch you something you've already rejected.
{{firstName|Hi}} — no comparison chart, I promise. If you want, I'll show you the one thing we do differently and you can tell me whether it matters.
Ten minutes, {{firstName|there}}, one difference, no slides. Worth it or shall I leave you to your shortlist?
I'll stop there, {{firstName|there}}. Genuinely hope whatever you pick works — come back if it doesn't.
Leaving it, {{firstName|there}}. If the tool you choose disappoints in six months, that's a fine time to talk.
